data: In which part of the image are there more blue circles?

The scatter plot shows three different types of data points represented by different shapes and colors: white circles for 19th-century poems, black triangles for Imagist poems, and dark blue circles for contemporary poems. The x-axis represents the publication year, and the y-axis represents the arousal score.

To determine where there are more blue circles, we need to look at the distribution of the dark blue circles across the y-axis. From the caption, we know that the contemporary poems are represented by dark blue circles. By visually inspecting the plot, we can see that the dark blue circles are more concentrated in the lower part of the y-axis, specifically around the range of 3.5 to 4.0. This indicates that there are more contemporary poems with lower arousal scores compared to the other two groups.

Therefore, the part of the image with more blue circles is the lower part of the y-axis.
